full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that the property in dispute belonged to one Rajab Ali who died leaving two sons namely Jalal Baksh and Aziz Baksh and also a widow named Surati Bibi. Jalal Baksh the elder son was very clever and intelligent and used to manage the household. The younger brother Aziz Baksh was on the other hand illiterate and had to depend upon his elder brother who was entrusted with the management of all the affairs of the family. Taking advantage of the illiteracy of Aziz Baksh and his dependence upon him Jalal Baksh got 11 annas 4 gondas share of the suit land recorded in his name, -/2/- annas in the name of Surati Bibi and -/2/- annas 16 gondas only in the name of Aziz Baksh in the C.S. Khatian without the knowledge and consent of Aziz Baksh. The said entries in the records of rights in respect of the shares of Jalal Baksh and Aziz Baksh were wrong as the shares of the two brothers in the properties left by their father were equal. Surati Bibi having died subsequently, Jalal Baksh and Aziz Baksh inherited her share equally. On the death of Jalal Baksh his properties were inherited by his 5 sons namely Defendant Nos. 1 to 5 and seven daughters, namely, Defendant No. 6 to 9 and 11 Kulsum Bibi, predecessor of Defendant Nos. 11 to 15 and Batashi Bibi, predecessor of Defendant Nos. 16 to 18, all of whom thus jointly inherited -/8/- annas share of the suit land. Thereafter Aziz Baksh died leaving behind 4 sons namely plaintiff Nos. 1 to 4 wife plaintiff No. 5 and three daughters, plaintiffs Nos. 6 to 8 who jointly inherited the remaining -/8/- annas of the land in suit. The disputed land was never partitioned by metes and bounds and the principal defendants who are in possession of the major portion of the suit land and have sold away some of the lands did not agree to partition the ejmali land in spite of the interest made by the plaintiffs. It has been also alleged that the wrong entries in the C.S. records have since been corrected on the basis of an application made on behalf of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs shares, totaling -/8/- as have been duty recorded in the new khatian after necessary correction. The proforma Defendants Nos. 20 to 26 are said to have purchased some of the lands in the suit. There was addition of a number of parties as defendants to the suit by the subsequent orders of the Court.
